sentences.zh: 郭璞

translations.literal: Guo Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 郭璞，字景純，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Guo Pu, courtesy Jingchun, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu, courtesy name Jingchun, came from Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 父瑗，尚書都令史。

translations.literal: His father Guo Yuan was secretary chief clerk of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Guo Yuan, served as secretary chief clerk of the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 時尚書杜預有所增損，瑗多駁正之，以公方著稱。

translations.literal: When Masters of Writing Du Yu made additions and cuts, Yuan frequently refuted and corrected him and became famed for impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Du Yu revised protocols Guo Yuan corrected his slips so steadily that contemporaries praised his fairness.

sentences.zh: 終於建平太守。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand Administrator of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as governor of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 璞好經術，博學有高才，而訥於言論，詞賦為中興之冠。

translations.literal: Pu loved classical studies, was broadly learned with lofty talent, yet clumsy in debate; his verse ranked first among the Restoration writers.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu loved classical learning and mastered many disciplines despite awkward speech; poets ranked his fu verse foremost among the Restoration authors.

sentences.zh: 好古文奇字，妙於陰陽算曆。

translations.literal: He loved antique script and unusual graphs and excelled at yin-yang reckoning and calendars.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished archaic characters and excelled at yin-yang numerology and calendar science.

sentences.zh: 有郭公者，客居河東，精于卜筮，璞從之受業。

translations.literal: There was a Master Guo who lodged west of the river and mastered divination; Pu studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: A visitor called Master Guo practiced divination west of the river, and Guo Pu apprenticed himself to him.

sentences.zh: 公以《青囊中書》九卷與之，由是遂洞五行、天文、卜筮之術，攘災轉禍，通致無方，雖京房、管輅不能過也。

translations.literal: The elder gave him nine fascicles of The Satchel of Azure Secrets; thereafter Pu penetrated the arts of the Five Agents, astronomy, and divination—averting calamity and shifting fortune without fixed method—even Jing Fang and Guan Lu could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: The master handed him nine volumes of The Satchel of Azure Secrets; Guo Pu thereby mastered the Five Agents, astronomy, and milfoil divination, turning aside disasters with uncanny ease—skills said to eclipse Jing Fang and Guan Lu.

sentences.zh: 璞門人趙載嘗竊《青襄書》，未及讀，而為火所焚。

translations.literal: Pu's disciple Zhao Zai once stole The Satchel of Azure Fragrance; before he could read it fire burned it.
translations.idiomatic: Disciple Zhao Zai once stole the azure satchel text; flames consumed it before he could open a page.

sentences.zh: 惠懷之際，河東先擾。

translations.literal: At the juncture of Hui and Huai emperors, Hedong was first disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Between Emperors Hui and Huai turmoil struck Hedong first.

sentences.zh: 璞筮之，投策而歎曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: Pu divined it; cast stalks and sighed: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu cast the milfoil, threw down the stalks, and cried: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 黔黎將湮於異類，桑梓其翦為龍荒乎！

translations.literal: Black-haired folk about to sink amid barbarians—homeland mulberries surely sheared into dragon wastes!
translations.idiomatic: The black-haired masses face extinction among foreign tribes; will our home mulberries be scythed into steppe waste?

sentences.zh: 」於是潛結姻昵及交遊數十家，欲避地東南。

translations.literal: Thereupon secretly bound marriage kin and travel friends several tens of houses—wished flee land southeast.
translations.idiomatic: He then quietly tied marriage ties and travel bonds with dozens of families, planning to escape southeast.

sentences.zh: 抵將軍趙固，會固所乘良馬死，固惜之，不接賓客。

translations.literal: He reached General Zhao Gu—happened Guo's ridden fine horse died—Guo prized it—did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: He came to General Zhao Gu while Zhao's prized mount had died; Zhao mourned the beast and refused visitors.

sentences.zh: 璞至，門吏不為通。

translations.literal: Pu arrived—gate clerks did not pass word.
translations.idiomatic: Gatekeepers barred Guo Pu when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「吾能活馬。

translations.literal: Pu said: I can revive the horse.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu announced: "I can bring that horse back to life.

sentences.zh: 」吏驚入白固。

translations.literal: Clerk astonished entered reported Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Startled guards rushed within to tell Zhao Gu.

sentences.zh: 固趨出，曰：「君能活吾馬乎？

translations.literal: Guo hurried out—said: Sir can revive my horse?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu hurried forth demanding: "Can you truly revive my horse?"

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「得健夫二三十人，皆持長竿，東行三十里，有丘林社廟者，便以竿打拍，當得一物，宜急持歸。

translations.literal: Pu said: Obtain sturdy fellows twenty-thirty men—all hold long poles—east go thirty li—where mound grove shrine spirits—then with poles strike drum—ought obtain one thing—fit urgently carry back.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu instructed: "Take twenty or thirty sturdy men with long poles. Thirty li east stand hills, woods, and village shrines; beat every shrine until something appears—snatch it and run home.

sentences.zh: 得此，馬活矣。

translations.literal: Obtain this—horse lives.
translations.idiomatic: Bring that thing here and the horse will rise."

sentences.zh: 」固如其言，果得一物似猴，持歸。

translations.literal: Guo acted as said—indeed obtained one thing resembling monkey—carried back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu obeyed; his men returned clutching a monkey-like creature.

sentences.zh: 此物見死馬，便噓吸其鼻。

translations.literal: This creature saw dead horse—then blew sucked its nose.
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the corpse it breathed into the nostrils.

sentences.zh: 頃之馬起，奮迅嘶鳴，食如常，不復見向物。

translations.literal: Shortly horse rose—sprang swift neighed—ate as usual—no longer saw former creature.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later the horse lurched up, neighed, and fed as always while the creature vanished.

sentences.zh: 固奇之，厚加資給。

translations.literal: Guo marvelled at him—greatly added provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu stood amazed and rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 行至廬江，太守胡孟康被丞相召為軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Going reached Lujiang—Grand Administrator Hu Mengkang was summoned by Chancellor as army advisory libationer.
translations.idiomatic: At Lujiang, Prefect Hu Mengkang received summons from the chancellor to serve as army counsellor and libationer.

sentences.zh: 時江淮清宴，孟康安之，無心南渡。

translations.literal: At time Jiang-Hai clear banquet—Mengkang settled it—no mind south crossing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi region seemed tranquil, so Hu rested easy and saw no need to flee south.

sentences.zh: 璞為占曰「敗」。

translations.literal: Pu for him divined saying Defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu cast lots for him and read defeat.

sentences.zh: 康不之信。

translations.literal: Kang did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mengkang refused to credit it.

sentences.zh: 璞將促裝去之，愛主人婢，無由而得，乃取小豆三斗，繞主人宅散之。

translations.literal: Pu about urge pack leave—loved master's slave girl—no means obtain—then took small beans three pecks—around master's house scattered them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu meant to pack out yet coveted his host's maid; unable to win her openly he scattered three pecks of beans around the compound.

sentences.zh: 主人晨見赤衣人數千圍其家，就視則滅，甚惡之，請璞為卦。

translations.literal: Master dawn saw red-clothed men thousand surround his house—approached looked then vanished—greatly hated it—begged Pu cast hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the host saw thousands of red figures ringing his halls; they vanished on approach. Uneasy, he asked Guo Pu for a reading.

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「君家不宜畜此婢，可于東南二十里賣之，慎勿爭價，則此妖可除也。

translations.literal: Pu said: Your house not fit raise this maid—may at southeast twenty li sell her—carefully do not haggle price—then this spectre can remove.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said: "You must not keep this servant—sell her twenty li southeast without bargaining and the haunting ends.

sentences.zh: 」主人從之。

translations.literal: Master followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The master complied.

sentences.zh: 璞陰令人賤買此婢。

translations.literal: Pu secretly ordered men cheap buy this maid.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu secretly sent buyers to purchase her cheap.

sentences.zh: 復為符投于井中，數千赤衣人皆反縛，一一自投于井，主人大悅。

translations.literal: Again made talisman cast into well—several thousand red-clothes men all reverse bound—one by one self cast into well—master greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped another charm into the well; thousands of red phantoms appeared bound hand and foot and plunged after it, delighting the host.

sentences.zh: 璞攜婢去。

translations.literal: Pu carried maid away.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu walked away with the girl.

sentences.zh: 後數旬而廬江陷。

translations.literal: After several tens ten-days then Lujiang fell.
translations.idiomatic: Within weeks Lujiang fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 璞既過江，宣城太守殷祐引為參軍。

translations.literal: Pu having crossed river—Xuancheng Grand Administrator Yin You led him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi Guo Pu joined Xuancheng prefect Yin You as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 時有物大如水牛，灰色卑腳，腳類象，胸前尾上皆白，大力而遲鈍，來到城下，眾咸異焉。

translations.literal: At time was creature large as water buffalo—grey low feet—feet like elephant—chest front tail top all white—great strength yet sluggish—came beneath walls—all marvelled.
translations.idiomatic: A beast as big as a buffalo—grey hide, stub legs like an elephant's, white chest and tail—strong but sluggish—appeared below the walls and amazed everyone.

sentences.zh: 祐使人伏而取之，令璞作卦，遇《遁》之《蠱》，其卦曰：「《艮》體連《乾》，其物壯巨。

translations.literal: You ordered men lie wait seize it—ordered Pu cast hexagram—met Dun toward Gu—the hexagram says: Gen body joins Qian—the creature stout huge.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You had it trapped and told Guo Pu to divine; the cast ran Retreat turning into Corruption: "Gen rests upon Qian—the beast is massive.

sentences.zh: 山潛之畜，匪兕匪武。

translations.literal: Mountain lurking beast—not rhino not martial.
translations.idiomatic: A creature lurking in the hills—neither rhinoceros nor tiger.

sentences.zh: 身與鬼並，精見二午。

translations.literal: Body with spirits together—essence sees two noon.
translations.idiomatic: Its body mingles ghosts; omens pair on the noon stems.

sentences.zh: 法當為禽，兩靈不許。

translations.literal: Rule ought become quarry—two spirits not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Justice names it prey, yet twin spirits withhold consent.

sentences.zh: 遂被一創，還其本墅。

translations.literal: Then suffers one wound—returns its native haunt.
translations.idiomatic: One wound drives it home to its mountain den.

sentences.zh: 按卦名之，是為驢鼠。

translations.literal: According hexagram name it—this is donkey-rat.
translations.idiomatic: Name it by the hexagram—call it the donkey-rat."

sentences.zh: 」卜適了，伏者以戟刺之，深尺餘，遂去不復見。

translations.literal: Divination just finished—ambushers with halberd stabbed it—deep over chi—then departed no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the reading ended ambushers thrust halberds a foot deep; the thing fled unseen.

sentences.zh: 郡綱紀上祠，請殺之。

translations.literal: Commandery clerk ascended shrine—begged kill it.
translations.idiomatic: County officers petitioned the shrine gods for permission to kill it.

sentences.zh: 巫云：「廟神不悅，曰：『此是䢼亭驢山君鼠，使詣荊山，暫來過我，不須觸之。

translations.literal: Shaman said: Temple god not pleased—says: This is Gongting Donkey Mountain lord rat—sent go Jing Mountain—temporarily came visit me—need not touch it.
translations.idiomatic: The medium reported the temple god displeased: "This is Lord Rat of Donkey Mountain at Gongting bound for Jing Mountain—only passing through—do not harm him.

sentences.zh: 』」其精妙如此。

translations.literal: Such subtle wonderful thus.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the finesse of Guo Pu's craft.

sentences.zh: 祐遷石頭督護，璞復隨之。

translations.literal: You transferred Stone Citadel protector—Pu again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin You moved to command Stone Citadel Guo Pu followed.

sentences.zh: 時有鼯鼠出延陵，璞占之曰：「此郡東當有妖人欲稱制者，尋亦自死矣。

translations.literal: At time flying squirrel emerged Yanling—Pu divined saying: This commandery east ought have freakish man wishes claim mandate—soon also self dies.
translations.idiomatic: When a giant flying squirrel appeared at Yanling Guo Pu foretold: "East of this commandery a sorcerer will seize the mandate—and soon perish.

sentences.zh: 後當有妖樹生，然若瑞而非瑞，辛螫之木也。

translations.literal: Later ought have freakish tree grow—yet like auspicious yet not auspicious—pungent sting tree.
translations.idiomatic: Later an uncanny tree will sprout—looking auspicious yet poisonous as nettles.

sentences.zh: 儻有此者，東南數百里必有作逆者，期明年矣。

translations.literal: If have this one—southeast several hundred li ought have rebellion-maker—deadline next year.
translations.idiomatic: Should it appear, rebels will stir within a few hundred li southeast within the coming year."

sentences.zh: 」無錫縣欻有茱萸四株交枝而生，若連理者，其年盜殺吳興太守袁琇。

translations.literal: Wuxi county suddenly had four cornus trees intertwining branches growing—as joined principle—that year bandits killed Wuxing Grand Administrator Yuan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cornus trees in Wuxi suddenly intertwined like paired trunks; that year bandits slew Wuxing prefect Yuan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 或以問璞，璞曰：「卯爻發而沴金，此木不曲直而成災也。

translations.literal: Someone used ask Pu—Pu said: Mao line issues yet harms metal—this wood not bend straight yet completes calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned later Guo Pu explained: "The Mao trigram stirs and injures metal—wood turns vicious instead of sheltering.

sentences.zh: 」王導深重之，引參己軍事。

translations.literal: Wang Dao deeply prized him—led join own military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao esteemed him and brought him onto staff.

sentences.zh: 嘗令作卦，璞言：「公有震厄，可命駕西出數十里，得一柏樹，截斷如身長，置常寢處，災當可消矣。

translations.literal: Once ordered cast hexagram—Pu said: Lord has thunder calamity—may order carriage west go several tens li—obtain one cypress tree—cut break like body length—place usual sleeping place—calamity ought vanish.
translations.idiomatic: Asked once to read Wang Dao's fate Guo Pu said: "Thunder threatens you—drive west several tens of li, fell a cypress your height, lay it where you sleep, and the omen lifts.

sentences.zh: 」導從其言。

translations.literal: Dao followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao obeyed.

sentences.zh: 數日果震，柏樹粉碎。

translations.literal: Several days indeed thunder—cypress tree smashed splintered.
translations.idiomatic: Days later lightning struck and shattered the timber.

sentences.zh: 時元帝初鎮鄴，導令璞筮之，遇《咸》之《井》，璞曰：「東北郡縣有『武』名者，當出鐸，以著受命之符。

translations.literal: At time Yuan Emperor first garrisoned Ye—Dao ordered Pu divine—met Xian toward Jing—Pu said: Northeast commanderies counties having Wu name—ought produce bell-clapper—to manifest receiving mandate token.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan Emperor still held Ye Wang Dao had Guo Pu cast lots; the hexagram ran Concord turning into Well: "A county northeast bearing the syllable Wu will yield bronze clappers proving Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 西南郡縣有『陽』名者，井當沸。

translations.literal: Southwest commanderies counties having Yang name—well ought boil.
translations.idiomatic: Where southwest counties bear Yang in their names village wells will boil."

sentences.zh: 」其後晉陵武進縣人于田中得銅鐸五枚，曆陽縣中井沸，經日乃止。

translations.literal: Afterward Jinling Wujin county men in fields obtained bronze clappers five pieces—Liyang county central wells boiled—passed days then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon peasants at Wujin in Jinling dug up five bronze bells while wells seethed in Liyang for days.

sentences.zh: 及帝為晉王，又使璞筮，遇《豫》之《睽》，璞曰：「會稽當出鐘，以告成功，上有勒銘，應在人家井泥中得之。

translations.literal: When Emperor became Jin king—again ordered Pu divine—met Yu toward Kui—Pu said: Kuaiji ought produce bell—to announce completion merit—top has carved inscription—response at people's home well mud within obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Rui became Jin prince Guo Pu cast again; Rest turning into Opposition foretold: "Kuaiji will yield a triumph bell bearing an inscription dredged from household wells.

sentences.zh: 繇辭所謂'先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝'者也。

translations.literal: Xi commentary so-called 'Former kings used making music honour virtue—richly present Supreme Lord' those.
translations.idiomatic: This matches Xi Ci's line that ancient kings shaped music to magnify virtue and offered it lavishly on high."

sentences.zh: 」及帝即位，太興初，會稽剡縣人果于井中得一鐘，長七寸二分，口徑四寸半，上有古文奇書十八字，云「會稽嶽命」，余字時人莫識之。

translations.literal: When Emperor ascended throne—Taixing early—Kuaiji Shan county men indeed in well obtained one bell—long seven cun two fen—mouth diameter four cun half—top had antique script strange graphs eighteen characters—said Kuaiji Peak Mandate—remainder characters contemporaries none recognized.
translations.idiomatic: After enthronement, early in Taixing, villagers of Shan county indeed pulled from a well a bell seven cun two fen long and four and a half cun wide engraved with eighteen archaic graphs reading Kuaiji Peak Mandate while other marks baffled everyone.

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「蓋王者之作，必有靈符，塞天人之心，與神物合契，然後可以言受命矣。

translations.literal: Pu said: Cover king's undertaking—must have spirit tally—block heaven man's hearts—with divine objects match tally—afterwards can speak receiving mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu declared: "True kings always earn spirit tallies that seal heaven and men's wills and align with sacred relics—only then may they speak of mandate.

sentences.zh: 觀五鐸啟號于晉陵，棧鐘告成於會稽，瑞不失類，出皆以方，豈不偉哉！

translations.literal: Observe five clappers open cry at Jinling—pile bell announce completion at Kuaiji—omens not miss classes—issue all by quarter—is it not grand!
translations.idiomatic: Five clappers hailed Jinling while Kuaiji's bell proclaimed completion—omens arrive by kind and quarter—is this not majestic!

sentences.zh: 若夫鐸發其響，鐘征其象，器以數臻，事以實應，天人之際不可不察。

translations.literal: As for clappers issue their sound—bells verify their images—vessels by number arrive—affairs by reality respond—heaven man boundary cannot not examine.
translations.idiomatic: Clappers sound the decree and bells manifest the image—implements arrive by number while deeds answer in fact—never neglect the hinge between heaven and man.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚重之。

translations.literal: Emperor greatly prized him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 璞著《江賦》，其辭甚偉，為世所稱。

translations.literal: Pu composed River Fu—its phrasing very grand—by age praised.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu's River Fu moved readers with its grandeur.

sentences.zh: 後復作《南郊賦》，帝見而嘉之，以為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Later again composed Southern Suburb Fu—Emperor saw and praised—made him collator-author aide.
translations.idiomatic: His Southern Suburb Fu delighted the throne and earned appointment as assistant editor.

sentences.zh: 于時陰陽錯繆，而刑獄繁興，璞上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time yin-yang astray—yet punishments prisons flourish rise—Pu submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: As yin and yang slipped out of phase and torture multiplied Guo Pu memorialized:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，優詔報之。

translations.literal: Memorial presented—gracious edict replied.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered with a gracious rescript.

sentences.zh: 其後日有黑氣，璞復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Afterward sun had black vapour—Pu again submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When black vapors veiled the sun he memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 頃之遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Shortly transferred Masters of Writing gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose to gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 數言便宜，多研匡益。

translations.literal: Repeatedly spoke convenience—many investigated aid profit.
translations.idiomatic: He tendered timely counsel that sharpened policy.

sentences.zh: 明帝之在東宮，與溫嶠、庾亮並有布衣之好，璞亦以才學見重，埒於嶠、亮，論者美之。

translations.literal: Ming Emperor's being Eastern Palace—with Wen Qiao, Yu Liang together had cloth-clothes friendship—Pu also by talent learning seen honoured—equal to Qiao, Liang—discoursers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: While Ming Emperor was heir Wen Qiao and Yu Liang enjoyed rustic friendship with him; Guo Pu matched them in scholarship and critics admired the pairing.

sentences.zh: 然性輕易，不修威儀，嗜酒好色，時或過度。

translations.literal: Yet nature light easy—did not cultivate awe deportment—loved wine loved beauty—times perhaps excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was careless of dignity, loved wine and women, and often overindulged.

sentences.zh: 著作郎干寶常誡之曰：「此非適性之道也。

translations.literal: Collator-author Gan Bao often warned him saying: This not suit nature's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Editor Gan Bao warned: "This cannot nourish your nature.

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「吾所受有本限，用之恆恐不得盡，卿乃憂酒色之為患乎！」

translations.literal: Pu said: What I receive has root limit—using always fear not obtain exhaust—you yet worry wine beauty becoming peril!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu replied: "My allotted span is finite—I fear exhausting life without tasting everything—and you fret over wine and beauty?"

sentences.zh: 璞既好卜筮，縉紳多笑之。

translations.literal: Pu since loved divination—gentry belts many laughed him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials mocked his obsession with divination.

sentences.zh: 又自以才高位卑，乃著《客傲》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Again self thought talent high position low—then composed Guest Arrogance—its phrasing says:
translations.idiomatic: Believing his gifts outstripped his rank he wrote Guest's Pride, whose text begins:

sentences.zh: ，皇孫生，璞上疏曰：

translations.literal: Imperial grandson born—Pu submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial grandson was born Guo Pu submitted:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，納焉，即大赦改年。

translations.literal: Memorial presented—accepted—then great amnesty changed era.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted it, proclaimed an amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 時暨陽人任穀因耕息於樹下，忽有一人著羽衣就淫之，既而不知所在，穀遂有娠。

translations.literal: At time Jiyang man Ren Gu because ploughed rested beneath tree—suddenly one man wearing feather robe approached violated him—afterward knew not whereabouts—Gu then had pregnancy.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiyang farmer named Ren Gu napped beneath a tree where a feather-robed stranger violated him and vanished; Ren Gu conceived.

sentences.zh: 積月將產，羽衣人復來，以刀穿其陰下，出一蛇子便去。

translations.literal: Months piled about birth—feather-robed man again came—with knife pierced his genitals below—issued one snake child then left.
translations.idiomatic: Months later as labour began the stranger returned, slit his groin, drew out a serpentling, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 谷遂成宦者。

translations.literal: Gu then became eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gu became a eunuch thereafter.

sentences.zh: 後詣闕上書，自雲有道術。

translations.literal: Later went palace gate memorialized—self claimed possessed Dao arts.
translations.idiomatic: Later he petitioned court boasting arcane arts.

sentences.zh: 帝留谷于宮中。

translations.literal: Emperor detained Gu within palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor housed Ren Gu inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 璞復上疏曰：「任穀所為妖異，無有因由。

translations.literal: Pu again memorialized saying: Ren Gu acts demon-anomaly—none cause origin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu wrote again: "Ren Gu's marvel lacks rational cause.

sentences.zh: 陛下玄鑒廣覽，欲知其情狀，引之禁內，供給安處。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dark mirror broad survey—wishes know its circumstance—led within forbidden interior—supply peaceful lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wished to study him and lodged him within the palace.

sentences.zh: 臣聞為國以禮正，不聞以奇邪。

translations.literal: Your servant hears ruling state by ritual rectitude—not hears by freakish wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: States stand on ritual rectitude, not occult strangeness.

sentences.zh: 所聽惟人，故神降之吉。

translations.literal: What heard only humans—therefore spirits descend auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Listen to men and spirits grant blessing.

sentences.zh: 陛下簡默居正，動遵典刑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty quiet silent dwell correct—actions follow canonical models.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules in austere silence and follows statute.

sentences.zh: 案《周禮》，奇服怪人不入宮，況穀妖詭怪人之甚者，而登講肆之堂，密邇殿省之側，塵點日月，穢亂天聽，臣之私情竊所以不取也。

translations.literal: According Zhou Ritual—strange clothes freakish men do not enter palace—how much more Gu demon deceit freakish man extreme ones—yet ascend lecture mart hall—close beside palace bureau flank—dust spots sun moon—filth confusion heaven hearing—your servant private feeling privately therefore not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rituals bar freakish dress and persons from palace gates—Ren Gu exceeds every freak yet lectures beside your halls; he soils daylight and befouls imperial ears—I cannot endorse him.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以谷信為神靈所憑者，則應敬而遠之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty if take Gu trust as spirits spirits rely—then ought respect yet distant.
translations.idiomatic: If you deem him spirit-possessed honour him from afar.

sentences.zh: 夫神，聰明正直，接以人事。

translations.literal: As for spirits—bright intelligent upright straight—receive with human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits are lucid and upright and approach through human affairs.

sentences.zh: 若以穀為妖蠱詐妄者，則當投畀裔土，不宜令褻近紫闈。

translations.literal: If take Gu as demon gu deceit false—then ought cast deliver wild lands—not fit allow irreverent near purple gate.
translations.idiomatic: If he is fraud banish him beyond the frontier—never seat him beside the purple gates.

sentences.zh: 若以穀或是神祇告譴、為國作眚者，則當克己修禮以弭其妖，不宜令谷安然自容，肆其邪變也。

translations.literal: If take Gu perhaps spirits announce reproach—for state make calamity—then ought restrain self cultivate ritual to end its demon—not fit allow Gu peaceful self tolerate—unleash its wicked transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If spirits warn through him discipline yourself with ritual to end the omen—do not let Ren Gu lounge here spreading corruption.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為陰陽陶烝，變化萬端，亦是狐狸魍魎憑假作慝。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks yin-yang pottery steam—transformations myriad ends—also are foxes wang-liang rely borrow commit evil.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish minister believes yin-yang ferments myriad shapes—often fox-spirits borrow flesh to work harm.

sentences.zh: 願陛下采臣愚懷，特遣穀出。

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty adopt servant foolish heart—especially dispatch Gu leave.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty heed this plea and send Ren Gu away from court.

sentences.zh: 臣以人乏，忝荷史任，敢忘直筆，惟義是規。

translations.literal: Servant because men lacking—shame bear historian duty—dare forget straight brush—only righteousness is rule.
translations.idiomatic: Though understaffed I bear the historian's shame—how dare I neglect honest ink or stray from duty.

sentences.zh: 」其後元帝崩，穀因亡走。

translations.literal: Afterward Yuan Emperor died—Gu therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Emperor died Ren Gu fled.

sentences.zh: 璞以母憂去職，卜葬地于暨陽，去水百步許。

translations.literal: Pu because mother's mourning left office—divined burial land at Jiyang—away water hundred paces about.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his mother Guo Pu quit office and chose a gravesite at Jiyang within a hundred paces of the river.

sentences.zh: 人以近水為言，璞曰：「當即為陸矣。

translations.literal: People used near water as warning—Pu said: Soon will become dry land.
translations.idiomatic: Critics warned it stood too close to water; Guo Pu replied: "It will soon lie far inland.

sentences.zh: 」其後沙漲，去墓數十里皆為桑田。

translations.literal: Afterward sand rose—away tomb several tens li all became mulberry fields.
translations.idiomatic: Later silt piled until mulberry orchards stretched tens of li beyond the tomb.

sentences.zh: 未期，王敦起璞為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Before deadline—Wang Dun raised Pu as secretary aide.
translations.idiomatic: Before the period elapsed Wang Dun summoned him as secretary of headquarters.

sentences.zh: 是時潁川陳述為大將軍掾，有美名，為敦所重，未幾而沒。

translations.literal: At time Yingchuan Chen Shu was grand general aide—had fair fame—prized by Dun—not long then died.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan's Chen Shu served Wang Dun as aide-in-chief with shining reputation but died soon after.

sentences.zh: 璞哭之哀甚，呼曰：「嗣祖，嗣祖，焉知非福！

translations.literal: Pu wept him mournfully—called: Sizu, Sizu—how know not fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu mourned bitterly: "Sizu, Sizu—who says death brings no blessing?

sentences.zh: 」夫幾而敦作難。

translations.literal: Not long then Dun raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Dun rebelled.

sentences.zh: 時明帝即位逾年，未改號，而熒惑守房。

translations.literal: At time Ming Emperor ascended past year—had not changed era—yet Mars lodged in Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Emperor had reigned a year without changing the era name while Mars stalled in the Chamber mansion.

sentences.zh: 璞時休歸，帝乃遣使齎手詔問璞。

translations.literal: Pu at time rested returned—Emperor then dispatched envoy bear handwritten edict ask Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu was home on leave when couriers arrived with the emperor's handwritten questions.

sentences.zh: 會暨陽縣復上言曰赤烏見。

translations.literal: Happened Jiyang county again upward spoke saying red crow appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyang county reported crimson crows.

sentences.zh: 璞乃上疏請改年肆赦，文多不載。

translations.literal: Pu then upward memorial begged change era grant amnesty—text much not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu memorialized for a new era name and blanket amnesty—the full text is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 璞嘗為人葬，帝微服往觀之，因問主人何以葬龍角，此法當滅族。

translations.literal: Pu once buried someone—Emperor disguised went observe—thereupon asked master why bury dragon horn—this law ought extinguish clan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu once directed a burial that Ming Emperor inspected incognito; he challenged the host for burying on dragon horns—a prescription for clan extinction.

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「郭璞雲此葬龍耳，不出三年當致天子也。

translations.literal: Master said: Guo Pu says this buries dragon ears—within three years ought summon Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The host answered: "Guo Pu called this the dragon's ear—within three years it draws the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「出天子邪？

translations.literal: Emperor said: Produce Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "It produces an emperor?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「能致天子問耳。

translations.literal: Answered: Able summon Son of Heaven inquire ear.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu explained: "It draws the emperor to ask directions.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚異之。

translations.literal: Emperor greatly marvelled him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marvelled.

sentences.zh: 璞素與桓彝友善，彝每造之，或值璞在婦間，便入。

translations.literal: Pu by nature friendly with Huan Yi—Yi each visited him—or happened Pu among wives—then entered.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu befriended Huan Yi, who walked in unannounced even when Guo was among his women.

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「卿來，他處自可徑前，但不可廁上相尋耳。

translations.literal: Pu said: You come—elsewhere self may go straight forward—but may not on privy mutually seek ear.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu warned: "Elsewhere enter freely—never search me out in the privy.

sentences.zh: 必客主有殃。

translations.literal: Certainly guest host has calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Doing so brings disaster on host and guest.

sentences.zh: 」彝後因醉詣璞，正逢在廁，掩而觀之，見璞裸身被髮，銜刀設醊。

translations.literal: Yi afterward because drunk visited Pu—happened met on privy—screened observed—saw Pu naked body loose hair—bite knife set offering.
translations.idiomatic: Later a drunken Huan Yi peeked into the latrine and saw Guo Pu naked, hair loose, biting a blade before an altar.

sentences.zh: 璞見彝，撫心大驚曰：「吾每屬卿勿來，反更如是！

translations.literal: Pu saw Yi—stroked heart greatly startled said: I always instructed you not come—instead even thus!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu clutched his chest: "I forbade you—and still you came!

sentences.zh: 非但禍吾，卿亦不免矣。

translations.literal: Not only harms me—you also not exempt.
translations.idiomatic: You doom yourself as well as me.

sentences.zh: 天實為之，將以誰咎！

translations.literal: Heaven truly makes this—will blame whom!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven ordains it—whom can we blame?

sentences.zh: 」璞終嬰王敦之禍，彝亦死蘇峻之難。

translations.literal: Pu ended suffered Wang Dun calamity—Yi also died Su Jun rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu fell to Wang Dun and Huan Yi died in Su Jun's coup.

sentences.zh: 王敦之謀逆也，溫嶠、庾亮使璞筮之，璞對不決。

translations.literal: Wang Dun's plotting rebellion—Wen Qiao, Yu Liang ordered Pu divine—Pu answered undecided.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun plotted rebellion Wen Qiao and Yu Liang asked Guo Pu to divine; he hedged.

sentences.zh: 嶠、亮復令占己之吉凶，璞曰：「大吉。

translations.literal: Qiao, Liang again ordered divine own auspicious inauspicious—Pu said: Great auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded their own fortunes and heard "great auspicious.

sentences.zh: 」嶠等退，相謂曰：「璞對不了，是不敢有言，或天奪敦魄。

translations.literal: Qiao etc. withdrew—mutually said: Pu answer undecided—is dare not have speech—or heaven steals Dun soul.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew whispering: "His silence feared frank speech—or heaven seized Wang Dun's wits.

sentences.zh: 今吾等與國家共舉大事，而璞雲大吉，是為舉事必有成也。

translations.literal: Now we etc. with state together raise great affair—yet Pu says great auspicious—is for raising affair must have success.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guo Pu blessed our coup—signal victory.

sentences.zh: 」於是勸帝討敦。

translations.literal: Thereupon urged Emperor punish Dun.
translations.idiomatic: They urged Ming Emperor to strike Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 初，璞每言「殺我者山宗」，至是果有姓崇者構璞於敦。

translations.literal: At first Pu each said 'Kill me mountain clan'—when arrived indeed someone surname Chong framed Pu before Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu once predicted "Mountain clan will kill me"—a man surnamed Chong—homophone for clan—slandered him to Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 敦將舉兵，又使璞筮。

translations.literal: Dun about raise troops—again ordered Pu divine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun prepared rebellion and ordered another casting.

sentences.zh: 璞曰：「無成。

translations.literal: Pu said: Without success.
translations.idiomatic: "No success," said Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 」敦固疑璞之勸嶠、亮，又聞卦凶，乃問璞曰；

translations.literal: Dun firmly suspected Pu's urging Qiao, Liang—again heard hexagram ill—then asked Pu saying:
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious of Guo Pu's loyalty to Wen Qiao and Yu Liang and hearing ill omens Wang Dun demanded:

sentences.zh: 「卿更筮吾壽幾何？

translations.literal: Sir again divine my lifespan how much?
translations.idiomatic: "Cast again—how long do I live?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「思向卦，明公起事，必禍不久。

translations.literal: Answered: Thinking toward hexagram—Illustrious Duke raises affair—must calamity not long.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu replied: "Your former hexagram promises swift disaster once you move.

sentences.zh: 若住武昌，壽不可測。

translations.literal: If stay Wuchang—lifespan cannot measure.
translations.idiomatic: Remain at Wuchang and no one can reckon your years.

sentences.zh: 」敦大怒曰：「卿壽幾何？

translations.literal: Dun greatly angry said: Sir lifespan how much?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun raged: "And your span?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「命盡今日日中。

translations.literal: Said: Fate exhausts today noon.
translations.idiomatic: "It ends at noon today.

sentences.zh: 」敦怒，收璞，詣南岡斬之。

translations.literal: Dun angry—seized Pu—went South Ridge beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun seized Guo Pu and marched him to South Ridge for execution.

sentences.zh: 璞臨出，謂行刑者欲何之。

translations.literal: Pu about exit—asked executioner intend where.
translations.idiomatic: Walking out Guo Pu asked where they headed.

sentences.zh: 曰：「南岡頭。

translations.literal: Said: South ridge head.
translations.idiomatic: "South Ridge crest.

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「必在雙柏樹下。

translations.literal: Pu said: Certainly beneath paired cypress trees.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said: "Under twin cypresses.

sentences.zh: 」既至，果然。

translations.literal: Having arrived—indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: They found exactly that.

sentences.zh: 復云：「此樹應有大鵲巢。

translations.literal: Again said: This tree ought have great magpie nest.
translations.idiomatic: "There should be a giant magpie nest overhead.

sentences.zh: 」眾索之不得。

translations.literal: Crowd searched it—not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Searchers found nothing.

sentences.zh: 璞更令尋覓，果於枝間得一大鵲巢，密葉蔽之。

translations.literal: Pu further ordered seek—indeed on branches obtained one great magpie nest—dense leaves concealed it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu pointed higher; they found a huge nest hidden in the canopy.

sentences.zh: 初，璞中興初行經越城，間遇一人，呼其姓名，因以袴褶遺之。

translations.literal: At first Pu Restoration early travelled passed Yue city—between met one man—called his name—thereby with trousers jacket gifted him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Restoration Guo Pu crossed Yue City, hailed a stranger by name, and gave him riding clothes.

sentences.zh: 其人辭不受，璞曰：「但取，後自當知。

translations.literal: That man declined not accept—Pu said: Only take—later self ought know.
translations.idiomatic: The man refused until Guo Pu insisted he take them—"you will understand.

sentences.zh: 」其人遂受而去。

translations.literal: That man then accepted and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The stranger accepted and left.

sentences.zh: 至是，果此人行刑。

translations.literal: When arrived—indeed this man carried out execution.
translations.idiomatic: That same man later wielded the headsman's blade.

sentences.zh: 時年四十九。

translations.literal: Age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 及王敦平，追贈弘農太守。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun pacified—posthumously gifted Hongnong Grand Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun fell the court posthumously named him governor of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 初，庾翼幼時嘗令璞筮公家及身，卦成，曰：「建元之末丘山傾，長順之初子凋零。

translations.literal: At first Yu Yi childhood once ordered Pu divine ducal house and self—hexagram completed—said: Jianyuan end hills mountains collapse—Changshun beginning sons wither.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood Yu Yi asked Guo Pu to read his clan's fate: "When Jianyuan ends hills crumble; when Changshun begins sons perish.

sentences.zh: 」及康帝即位，將改元為建元，或謂庾冰曰：「子忘郭生之言邪？

translations.literal: When Kang Emperor ascended throne—about change era to Jianyuan—someone told Yu Bing: Son forgot Guo master's words?
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Emperor wished to adopt Jianyuan advisers reminded Yu Bing of Guo Pu's warning.

sentences.zh: 丘山上名，此號不宜用。

translations.literal: Hills mountains upper name—this title not fit use.
translations.idiomatic: "Jian pairs with hills—avoid that reign name.

sentences.zh: 」冰撫心歎恨。

translations.literal: Bing stroked heart sighed regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing smote his breast in regret.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，何充改元為永和，庾翼歎曰：「天道精微，乃當如是。

translations.literal: When Emperor died—He Chong changed era to Yonghe—Yu Yi sighed saying: Heaven Way subtle refined—then ought thus.
translations.idiomatic: After Kang Emperor died He Chong chose Yonghe; Yu Yi sighed: "Heaven's calculus is subtle indeed.

sentences.zh: 長順者，永和也，吾庸得免乎！

translations.literal: Changshun—Yonghe—I how escape!
translations.idiomatic: "Changshun meant Yonghe—how can I survive?

sentences.zh: 」其年翼卒。

translations.literal: That year Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi died that year.

sentences.zh: 冰又令筮其後嗣，卦成，曰：「卿諸子並當貴盛，然有白龍者，凶徵至矣。

translations.literal: Bing again ordered divine posterity—hexagram completed—said: Your sons together ought noble flourishing—yet who white dragon—ominous sign arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing asked about heirs: "Your sons will flourish yet beware the white dragon.

sentences.zh: 若墓碑生金，庾氏之大忌也。

translations.literal: If tombstone grows metal—Yu clan great taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Metal sprouting on a Yu tomb spells doom.

sentences.zh: 」後冰子蘊為廣州刺史，妾房內忽有一新生白狗子，莫知所由來，其妾秘愛之，不令蘊知。

translations.literal: Later Bing son Yun became Guangzhou prefect—concubine chamber inside suddenly had one newborn white puppy—none knew whence—concubine secretly loved—did not let Yun know.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing's son Yu Yun governed Guangzhou where a concubine secretly raised a newborn white pup.

sentences.zh: 狗轉長大，蘊入，是狗眉眼分明，又身至長而弱，異于常狗，蘊甚怪之。

translations.literal: Dog gradually grew large—Yun entered—this dog eyebrows eyes distinct—again body arrived long yet weak—different from usual dogs—Yun greatly marvelled.
translations.idiomatic: It grew oddly human in face yet weak in limb until Yu Yun noticed.

sentences.zh: 將出，共視在眾人前，忽失所在。

translations.literal: About exit—together viewed before crowd—suddenly lost whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yun drew it before witnesses it vanished.

sentences.zh: 蘊慨然曰：「殆白龍乎！

translations.literal: Yun sighed: Probably white dragon!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yun cried: "The white dragon!

sentences.zh: 庾氏禍至矣。

translations.literal: Yu clan calamity arrives.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan's doom arrives.

sentences.zh: 」又墓碑生金。

translations.literal: Again tombstone grew metal.
translations.idiomatic: Metal later filmed their tombstones.

sentences.zh: 俄而為桓溫所滅，終如其言。

translations.literal: Shortly by Huan Wen extinguished—ended like his words.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen soon wiped them out as predicted.

sentences.zh: 璞之占驗，皆如此類也。

translations.literal: Pu's divination verification—all like this category.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu's auguries ran true in such cases.

sentences.zh: 璞撰前後筮驗六十餘事，名為《洞林》。

translations.literal: Pu composed front-back divination verification sixty-odd affairs—named Piercing Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu compiled sixty divination cases in Piercing the Forest.

sentences.zh: 又抄京、費諸家要最，更撰《新林》十篇、《卜韻》一篇。

translations.literal: Again excerpted Jing, Fei masters essentials—again composed New Forest ten chapters—Divination Rhymes one chapter.
translations.idiomatic: He excerpted Jing Fang and Fei Zhi and wrote New Forest in ten fascicles plus Rhymes for Divination.

sentences.zh: 注釋《爾雅》，別為《音義》、《圖譜》。

translations.literal: Annotated Erya—separately made Sounds Meanings—Charts Catalogue.
translations.idiomatic: He glossed Erya with separate pronunciations, meanings, and illustrations.

sentences.zh: 又注《三蒼》、《方言》、《穆天子傳》、《山海經》及《楚辭》、《子虛》、《上林賦》數十萬言，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: Again annotated Three Archives—Dialect—Mu Son of Heaven Travels—Mountains Seas Classic—and Chu Lyrics—Sir Vacuity—Upper Woods Fu several hundred thousand characters—all transmitted on age.
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated the Three Archives, Dialect, Travels of Mu Son of Heaven, Classic of Mountains and Seas, Chu Ci, Sir Vacuity, and Upper Woods Fu—hundreds of thousands of characters still circulating.

sentences.zh: 所作詩賦誄頌亦數萬言。

translations.literal: Composed poems fu elegies eulogies also several tens thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: His poems, fu, elegies, and encomia ran tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 子驁，官至臨賀太守。

translations.literal: Son Ao—office reached Linhe Grand Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo Ao rose to governor of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 葛洪

translations.literal: Ge Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Ge Hong.

sentences.zh: 葛洪，字稚川，丹陽句容人也。

translations.literal: Ge Hong, courtesy Zhichuan—was man of Jurong in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong, courtesy name Zhichuan, came from Jurong in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖系，吳大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Ancestor Xi—Wu era Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Ge Xi served Wu as grand herald.

sentences.zh: 父悌，吳平後入晉，為邵陵太守。

translations.literal: Father Ti—after Wu pacified entered Jin—became Shaoling Grand Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ge Ti entered Jin service after Wu fell and governed Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 洪少好學，家貧，躬自伐薪以貿紙筆，夜輒寫書誦習，遂以儒學知名。

translations.literal: Hong youth loved learning—family poor—personally chopped firewood trade paper brush—night always wrote books recite practice—thereupon by Ru learning known.
translations.idiomatic: Poor yet diligent Ge Hong chopped fuel to buy paper, copying texts by night until scholars noted him.

sentences.zh: 性寡欲，無所愛玩，不知棋局幾道，摴蒱齒名。

translations.literal: Nature few desires—nothing loved play—did not know chess board how many lines—chupu tooth names.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked worldly cravings—never learned chess lines or dice names.

sentences.zh: 為人木訥，不好榮利，閉門卻掃，未嘗交遊。

translations.literal: As person wooden clumsy—did not love glory profit—closed gate swept courtyard—never travelled socialize.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn and uninterested in fame he barred his gate and seldom socialized.

sentences.zh: 于余杭山見何幼道、郭文舉，目擊而已，各無所言。

translations.literal: At Yuhang mountain saw He Youdao, Guo Wenju—eye witnessed only—each without speech.
translations.idiomatic: On Yuhang Mountain he met He Youdao and Guo Wenju—they exchanged only glances.

sentences.zh: 時或尋書問義，不遠數千里崎嶇冒涉，期於必得，遂究覽典籍，尤好神仙導養之法。

translations.literal: Sometimes sought books asked meanings—not far several thousand li rugged risk ford—deadline must obtain—thereupon thoroughly perused canons—especially loved transcendents guiding nourishment arts.
translations.idiomatic: He travelled thousands of li for obscure texts and mastered arcana, loving transcendental self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 從祖玄，吳時學道得仙，號曰葛仙公，以其練丹秘術授弟子鄭隱。

translations.literal: Granduncle Xuan—Wu time studied Dao attained transcendence—styled Ge Immortal Duke—with his cinnabar refining secret arts taught disciple Zheng Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His granduncle Ge Xuan became famed Ge Immortal Duke and passed cinnabar secrets to Zheng Yin.

sentences.zh: 洪就隱學，悉得其法焉。

translations.literal: Hong approached Yin studied—fully obtained his methods.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong studied under Zheng Yin and mastered every technique.

sentences.zh: 後師事南海太守上党鮑玄。

translations.literal: Later served as disciple Nanhai Grand Administrator Shangdang Bao Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under Nanhai prefect Bao Xuan of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 玄亦內學，逆占將來，見洪深重之，以女妻洪。

translations.literal: Xuan also interior learning—inverse divined future—saw Hong deeply prized him—with daughter wife Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan practiced interior arcana, foresaw Ge Hong's greatness, and married him his daughter.

sentences.zh: 洪傳玄業，兼綜練醫術，凡所著撰，皆精核是非，而才章富贍。

translations.literal: Hong transmitted Xuan enterprise—also synthesized refined medicine arts—whatever composed—all refined examine right wrong—yet talent chapters rich abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong inherited Bao's arts and medicine; every treatise weighed evidence yet read elegantly.

sentences.zh: 太安中，石冰作亂，吳興太守顧秘為義軍都督，與周玘等起兵討之，秘檄洪為將兵都尉，攻冰別率，破之，遷伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Taian within—Shi Bing raised rebellion—Wuxing Grand Administrator Gu Mi became righteous army commander-in-chief—with Zhou Qi etc. raised troops punish—Mi proclamation Hong as command troops commandant—attacked Bing detached force—broke them—transferred Wave-Cutting general.
translations.idiomatic: During Taian Ge Hong joined Gu Mi's loyal army against Shi Bing as commandant, routed a column, and earned promotion to Wave-Pacifying general.

sentences.zh: 冰平，洪不論功賞，徑至洛陽，欲搜求異書以廣其學。

translations.literal: Bing pacified—Hong not discussed merit rewards—straight went Luoyang—wished search unusual books broaden studies.
translations.idiomatic: After victory Ge Hong spurned rewards and hurried to Luoyang hunting rare books.

sentences.zh: 洪見天下已亂，欲避地南土，乃參廣州刺史嵇含軍事。

translations.literal: Hong saw realm already chaotic—wished flee land southern soil—then joined Guangzhou Inspector Xi Han military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing chaos Ge Hong joined Guangzhou Inspector Xi Han's staff seeking refuge south.

sentences.zh: 及含遇害，遂停南土多年，征鎮檄命一無所就。

translations.literal: When Han murdered—then halted southern soil many years—campaign defend proclamations orders none accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Han's murder stranded Ge Hong for years; he spurned every summons.

sentences.zh: 後還鄉里，禮辟皆不赴。

translations.literal: Later returned village—ritual summons none attended.
translations.idiomatic: Even recalled home he refused appointments.

sentences.zh: 元帝為丞相，辟為掾。

translations.literal: Yuan Emperor was Chancellor—summoned as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui was chancellor Ge Hong accepted aide duty.

sentences.zh: 以平賊功，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Because pacify bandit merit—gifted rank secondary marquis within passes.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing bandits brought him secondary marquis rank.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，司徒導召補州主簿，轉司徒掾，遷諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Xianhe early—Minister Tutor Dao summoned supplement prefecture chief clerk—transferred Chancellor aide—transferred consultant aide.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe Wang Dao named him prefect clerk, then chancellor aide, then consultant.

sentences.zh: 干寶深相親友，薦洪才堪國史，選為散騎常侍，領大著作，洪固辭不就。

translations.literal: Gan Bao deeply befriended him—recommended Hong talent fit national history—selected as attendant-in-ordinary—held chief compilation—Hong firmly declined not take.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao befriended Ge Hong and nominated him for court historian; the court named him supernumerary palace attendant and chief editor but Ge Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 以年老，欲練丹以祈遐壽，聞交阯出丹，求為句漏令。

translations.literal: Because aged—wished refine cinnabar pray long life—heard Jiaozhi produced cinnabar—begged become Gou Lou magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Aging, he sought cinnabar for longevity; learning Jiaozhi yielded ore he asked for the magistracy of Gou Lou.

sentences.zh: 帝以洪資高，不許。

translations.literal: Emperor because Hong stature high—not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, deeming him too eminent.

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「非欲為榮，以有丹耳。

translations.literal: Hong said: Not desire glory—because has cinnabar ear.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong answered: "I seek the elixir, not rank.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 洪遂將子侄俱行。

translations.literal: Hong then led sons nephews together travel.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong took sons and nephews along.

sentences.zh: 至廣州，刺史鄧岳留不聽去，洪乃止羅浮山煉丹。

translations.literal: Reached Guangzhou—Inspector Deng Yue detained not listen leave—Hong then halted Mount Luofu refine cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Deng Yue detained him; Ge Hong stayed on Mount Luofu to compound elixirs.

sentences.zh: 岳表補東官太守，又辭不就。

translations.literal: Yue memorial supplemented Eastern Office Grand Administrator—again declined not take.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue petitioned him as governor of Eastern Office yet again he declined.

sentences.zh: 岳乃以洪兄子望為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Yue then took Hong elder-brother son Wang as secretary aide.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue instead appointed Ge Hong's nephew Ge Wang secretary.

sentences.zh: 在山積年，優遊閑養，著述不輟。

translations.literal: Within mountains piled years—leisurely roamed idle nourish—writings never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Years on the mountain passed in serene study and ceaseless writing.

sentences.zh: 其自序曰：

translations.literal: His self-preface said:
translations.idiomatic: His own preface reads:

sentences.zh: 洪體乏進趣之才，偶好無為之業。

translations.literal: Hong body lacks advancing zest talent—accidentally loves non-action enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong admits no zeal for climbing office—only love of quiet non-action.

sentences.zh: 假令奮翅則能陵厲玄霄，騁足則能追風躡景，猶欲戢勁翮于於鷦鷃之群，藏逸跡於跛驢之伍，豈況大塊稟我以尋常之短羽，造化假我以至駑之蹇足？

translations.literal: Supposing order flap wings then can scale mystic empyrean—gallop feet then can chase wind tread brilliance—still wishes fold strong pinions amid quail flocks—hide fleet traces among lame donkeys—how mention great clod endows me common short feathers—creation lends me utmost dull lame feet?
translations.idiomatic: Had I wings to pierce the clouds or legs to outrun the gale, I would still hide among quails and limping asses—how much more when heaven gives me ordinary plumage and Creation fits me with stumbling hooves?

sentences.zh: 自卜者審，不能者止，又豈敢力蒼蠅而慕沖天之舉，策跛鱉而追飛兔之軌；

translations.literal: Self diviners examine—cannot ones stop—again how dare force blue-bottle admire sky-soaring deed—spur lame turtle pursue flying hare track;
translations.idiomatic: The wise know their limits; how may a fly aspire aloft or a lame tortoise chase the swiftest hare?

sentences.zh: 飾嫫母之篤陋，求媒陽之美談；

translations.literal: Adorn Mother Mo's deep ugliness—seek match Yang fair praise;
translations.idiomatic: Painting Mother Mo and expecting Yangzhou beauties to praise it—

sentences.zh: 推沙礫之賤質，索千金于和肆哉！

translations.literal: Push sand-gravel's mean substance—seek thousand gold at He market!
translations.idiomatic: —peddling gravel for jade prices in the He market!

sentences.zh: 夫僬僥之步而企及誇父之蹤，近才所以躓礙也；

translations.literal: As Jiaoyao's stride yet stands atop Kuafu's trace—modest talent therefore trips obstructs;
translations.idiomatic: A dwarf aping Kuafu's stride only trips—

sentences.zh: 要離之羸而強赴扛鼎之勢，秦人所以斷筋也。

translations.literal: Yaoli's frail yet strong rush cauldron-lifting force—Qin men therefore sever sinews.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Li lifting tripods broke Qin men's sinews—

sentences.zh: 是以望絕于榮華之途，而志安乎窮圮之域；

translations.literal: Therefore hope cut at glory-flower path—while intent rests in ruined waste realm;
translations.idiomatic: So I abandon ambition on glory's road and rest content in mean lanes;

sentences.zh: 藜藿有八珍之甘，蓬蓽有藻棁之樂也。

translations.literal: Chenopodium has eight-treasure sweetness—hawthorn door has jewelled-rafter joy.
translations.idiomatic: wild greens taste royal fare and hovels bring palace joy.

sentences.zh: 故權貴之家，雖咫尺弗從也；

translations.literal: Therefore power-noble houses—though cubits near not follow;
translations.idiomatic: Mighty houses inches away I shun;

sentences.zh: 知道之士，雖艱遠必造也。

translations.literal: knowing-Dao gentlemen—though hardship far must visit.
translations.idiomatic: men of the Way, however distant, I seek.

sentences.zh: 考覽奇書，既不少矣，率多隱語，難可卒解，自非至精不能尋究，自非篤勤不能悉見也。

translations.literal: Examined perused wonder books—already not few—mostly many hidden language—hard complete sudden solve—if not utmost refined cannot search investigate—if not utmost diligent cannot fully see.
translations.idiomatic: Strange books abound in riddles; without utmost wit and toil none masters them.

sentences.zh: 道士弘博洽聞者寡，而意斷妄說者眾。

translations.literal: Daoist masters vast learned hear few—yet opinion-cut reckless speak many.
translations.idiomatic: Few priests read widely while rash guesswork spreads.

sentences.zh: 至於時有好事者，欲有所修為，倉卒不知所從，而意之所疑又無足諮。

translations.literal: As for times have fond-affair ones—wish have cultivate acts—hasty not know follow what—while intent doubt again none consult.
translations.idiomatic: Would-be adepts rush unsure whom to ask.

sentences.zh: 今為此書，粗舉長生之理。

translations.literal: Now compose this book—roughly raise long-life principle.
translations.idiomatic: This book sketches the principles of longevity.

sentences.zh: 其至妙者不得宣之於翰墨，蓋粗言較略以示一隅，冀悱憤之徒省之可以思過半矣。

translations.literal: Utmost wondrous cannot declare on ink—cover rough words compare outline show one corner—hope troubled hearts save can think half beyond.
translations.idiomatic: The subtlest teachings resist ink; here is a sketch so earnest readers grasp half the lesson.

sentences.zh: 豈謂暗塞必能窮微暢遠乎，聊論其所先覺者耳。

translations.literal: How say blocked obscurity surely exhaust subtle extend far—merely discuss those first awakened ear.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot expose every mystery—only what I already perceive.

sentences.zh: 世儒徒知服膺周孔，莫信神仙之書，不但大而笑之，又將謗毀真正。

translations.literal: Age Ruists vainly know embrace Zhou Kong—none trust transcendents' books—not only great laugh them—again will slander true orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians mock immortal scriptures—some even slander the true teaching.

sentences.zh: 故予所著子言黃白之事，名曰《內篇》，其餘駁難通釋，名曰《外篇》，大凡內外一百一十六篇。

translations.literal: Therefore my composed masters speak yellow-white affairs—named Inner Chapters—remainder refute difficult interpret—named Outer Chapters—generally inner-outer hundred sixteen chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Hence my Inner Chapters on alchemy and Outer Chapters of debate—116 chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 雖不足藏諸名山，且欲緘之金匱，以示識者。

translations.literal: Although not enough hide famous mountains—yet wish seal metal cabinet—show knowing ones.
translations.idiomatic: They may not merit mountain vaults but deserve a golden coffer for discerning eyes.

sentences.zh: 自號抱樸子，因以名書。

translations.literal: Self-styled Master Embracing Simplicity—thereby named book.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Master Embracing Simplicity and titled his book accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其餘所著碑誄詩賦百卷，移檄章表三十卷，神仙、良吏、隱逸、集異等傳各十卷，又抄《五經》、《史》、《漢》、百家之言、方技雜事三百一十卷，《金匱藥方》一百卷，《肘後要急方》四卷。

translations.literal: Remainder composed stele elegies poems fu hundred fascicles—dispatches memorials thirty fascicles—transcendent, good magistrate, recluse, collected marvel biographies each ten fascicles—again excerpt Five Classics, Histories, Han, hundred masters, arts-medley affairs three hundred ten fascicles—Metal Casket Formulas hundred fascicles—Elbow-Lair Emergency Formulas four fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Besides a hundred fascicles of verse and prose, thirty of state papers, and ten each on transcendents, worthy magistrates, recluses, and marvels, he copied 310 fascicles of classics, histories, and technical lore, 100 of Metal Casket Formulas, and 4 of Emergency Formulas from the Elbow Lair.

sentences.zh: 洪博聞深洽，江左絕倫。

translations.literal: Hong vast hear deep unite—Jiang left unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong's erudition was unrivalled south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 著述篇章富於班馬，又精辯玄賾，析理入微。

translations.literal: Writings chapters richer than Ban Ma—again refined debate dark profound—split principle enter subtle.
translations.idiomatic: His corpus outbulked Ban and Sima and dissected arcana to the finest grain.

sentences.zh: 後忽與嶽疏云：「當遠行尋師，克期便發。

translations.literal: Later suddenly with Yue memorial said: About travel far seek teacher—fixed date then depart.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he wrote Deng Yue that he must journey for a teacher and would leave on schedule.

sentences.zh: 」嶽得疏，狼狽往別。

translations.literal: Yue obtained memorial—flustered went bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue rushed to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 而洪坐至日中，兀然若睡而卒，嶽至，遂不及見。

translations.literal: Yet Hong sat until noon—silent as sleep then died—Yue arrived—therefore not reach see.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong sat motionless like sleep until noon and died before Deng Yue arrived.

sentences.zh: 時年八十一。

translations.literal: Age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 視其顏色如生，體亦柔軟，舉屍入棺，甚輕，如空衣，世以為屍解得仙雲。

translations.literal: View his complexion like life—body also soft—lift corpse into coffin—very light—as empty clothes—age thought corpse-release attained transcendence cloud.
translations.idiomatic: His colour stayed lifelike, his limbs supple; lifted into the coffin he weighed like empty clothes—people called it corpse liberation and transcendence.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historians' Comment】
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：景純篤志綈緗，洽聞強記，在異書而畢綜，瞻往滯而咸釋；

translations.literal: Historians say: Jingchun devoted archives silk—hears widely remembers strong—in strange books wholly surveyed—gazed past obscurities all released;
translations.idiomatic: The historians say: Guo Pu devoted himself to silk tomes, remembered all he read, mastered exotic texts, and cleared every crux;

sentences.zh: 情源秀逸，思業高奇；

translations.literal: Feeling source elegant drift—thought enterprise lofty strange;
translations.idiomatic: his spirit flowed refined and his ideas soared;

sentences.zh: 襲文雅於西朝，振辭鋒于南夏，為中興才學之宗矣。

translations.literal: Inherited literary elegance Western Jin—vibrated rhetoric blade southern summer—became Restoration talent-learning ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: he inherited Western Jin letters and led southern literature—the patriarch of Restoration letters.

sentences.zh: 夫語怪征神，伎成則賤，前修貽訓，鄙乎茲道。

translations.literal: As for speaking weird summon gods—craft accomplished then base—former worthies left lessons—despise this path.
translations.idiomatic: Tales of spirits win cheap fame once skill turns stale—ancient teachers warned us to scorn such arts.

sentences.zh: 景純之探策定數，考往知來，邁京管於前圖，軼梓窀於遐篆。

translations.literal: Jingchun's exploring stalks fixed fate—examining past know coming—surpasses Jing-Guan former charts—surpasses Zi Shen remote seal-script.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guo Pu's stalk divining surpassed Jing Fang and Guan Lu and outdid astrologers like Zi Shen.

sentences.zh: 而宦微於世，禮薄于時，區區然寄《客傲》以申懷，斯亦伎成之累也。

translations.literal: Yet office minute in age—ritual thin in times—petty lodged Guest Arrogance declare heart—this also craft-accomplished burden.
translations.idiomatic: Office humbled him and ritual slighted him—hence his petty Guest's Pride—a burden of wasted craft.

sentences.zh: 若乃大塊流形，玄天賦命，吉凶修短，定乎自然。

translations.literal: If then great clod flows forms—dark heaven grants fate—auspicious ominous long short—settled in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Great Nature shapes forms and dark Heaven assigns spans—good or ill, long or short rest in what is natural.

sentences.zh: 雖稽象或通，而厭勝難恃，稟之有在，必也無差，自可居常待終，頹心委運，何至銜刀被髮，遑遑于穢向之間哉！

translations.literal: Although investigate images perhaps penetrate—yet apotropaic victory hard rely—endowment has fixed—must without error—self may dwell constant await end—sink heart entrust fate—why arrive bite blade loose hair—frantic amid filthy privies!
translations.idiomatic: Even divination may glimpse fate yet charms cannot be trusted—what is allotted cannot err—one may calmly await destiny—why bite blades and loose hair in frantic sorcery?

sentences.zh: 晚抗忠言，無救王敦之逆；

translations.literal: Late resisted loyal words—none rescue Wang Dun's rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Late loyal words could not stop Wang Dun's revolt;

sentences.zh: 初慚智免，竟斃「山宗」之謀。

translations.literal: First ashamed wise escape—finally killed 'mountain clan' plot.
translations.idiomatic: early wit spared him yet the "mountain clan" prophecy slew him.

sentences.zh: 仲尼所謂攻乎異端，斯害也已，悲夫！

translations.literal: Zhongni so-called attack strange ends—this harm also ended—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius warned against heterodox arts—their harm proves real—alas!

sentences.zh: 稚川束發從師，老而忘倦。

translations.literal: Zhichuan bound hair followed teacher—old yet forgot weary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichuan tied his hair and studied on, tireless in age.

sentences.zh: 紬奇冊府，總百代之遺編；

translations.literal: Draw out wonder archives—gather hundred generations lost compilations;
translations.idiomatic: He threaded marvel vaults and gathered generations of scattered writings;

sentences.zh: 紀化仙都，窮九丹之秘術。

translations.literal: Record transformations immortal capital—exhaust nine-cinnabar secret arts.
translations.idiomatic: he chronicled transcendence and plumbed the ninefold elixir.

sentences.zh: 謝浮榮而捐雜藝，賤尺寶而貴分陰，遊德棲真，超然事外。

translations.literal: Renounced floating glory cast miscellaneous arts—despise foot treasure honour inch shade—wander virtue dwell truth—transcend matters outside.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned vanity and baubles, prized each inch of time, roamed in virtue and lodged in truth beyond worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 全生之道，其最優乎！

translations.literal: Preserve life Way—its most excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Of ways to preserve life his was finest.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：景純通秀，夙振宏材。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Jingchun penetrates elegance—dawn shakes vast talent.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium sings: Jingchun's brilliance shone early and vast.

sentences.zh: 沈研鳥冊，洞曉龜枚。

translations.literal: Deep research bird tablets—thoroughly dawn turtle stalks.
translations.idiomatic: He plumbed omens of birds and turtles.

sentences.zh: 匪甯國釁，坐致身災。

translations.literal: Not only state calamity—sit causes body disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the state no grief yet met personal doom.

sentences.zh: 稚川優洽，貧而樂道。

translations.literal: Zhichuan superior unite—poor yet joyful Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichuan was learned though poor and rejoiced in the Way.

sentences.zh: 載范斯文，永傳洪藻。

translations.literal: Carries norm this pattern—forever transmit Hong brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: His pattern endures and his great letters shine on.
